t: Subsection (c) of section 11 of the Federal Reserve Act (12 U.S.C. 248(c)) is amended by striking both provisos, and by striking the last sentence, in such subsection.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that strikes provisos and a sentence from section 11(c) of the Federal Reserve Act. The tempting reading is that the struck text might have involved some outside-party process, but the section itself does not establish any consultation, hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue. No party outside the federal government is brought into a federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking both provisos, and by striking the last sentence, in such subsection.

qwen_block.w: This section is a purely technical amendment instruction that removes text from another statute. It does not establish any process for public comment, consultation with outside entities, or advisory boards. It merely changes the legal text of the Federal Reserve Act without describing any participatory mechanism.
qwen_block.s: Subsection (c) of section 11 of the Federal Reserve Act (12 U.S.C. 248(c)) is amended by striking both provisos, and by striking the last sentence, in such subsection.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that strikes both provisos and the last sentence from section 11(c) of the Federal Reserve Act. It sets up no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking power or right to sue involving anyone outside the federal government. Reading participation into it would require guessing at what the struck text said, and nothing in the section itself supports that.
opus.b: 1. **Reasoning.** The tempting reading is that because the section amends the Federal Reserve Act, it might affect some decision process that involves outside parties. That reading fails because the text only strikes two provisos and a sentence from 12 U.S.C. 248(c). It names no outside party, consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking power or right to sue. Nothing in it brings anyone from outside the federal government into a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section merely instructs the amendment of existing statutory text by removing specific provisos and a sentence. It does not establish any new mechanism for outside parties (such as the public, states, or experts) to consult with or participate in federal decision-making. The definition of participation requires active involvement of non-federal entities in the decision process, which is absent here.
qwen_chat.s: Subsection (c) of section 11 of the Federal Reserve Act (12 U.S.C. 248(c)) is amended by striking both provisos, and by striking the last sentence, in such subsection.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that amending the Federal Reserve Act could implicitly involve public participation if the removed text contained such provisions. However, the section itself only describes the legislative act of striking text; it does not establish any new process for outside parties to consult with or participate in federal decision-making. The definition requires the section itself to recommend or require participation (e.g., via comment periods, advisory boards with non-federal members, or consultation with states/tribes). This section is purely a textual amendment instruction.
